**Verdict: FAIL.** One required problem: the `file-display-loss` case can't pass as written. The shipping source itself looks correct. I only read the code and ran nothing. The focused cases that passed earlier predate this mode, so its failure here is reasoned from the code, not observed.

{
  "verdict": "FAIL",
  "requiredFindings": [
    {
      "id": "R1",
      "severity": "high",
      "file": "implementations/csharp/tests/fixtures/DiscoveryHost/FileRuntimeStartupFixture.cs",
      "line": 40,
      "problem": "The file-display-loss case uses the shared MaxEntryBytes = 16384, but its message is 8192 × U+200D. The captured JSONL needs at least 3 bytes per character (24576 > 16384), so EventEncoder.Encode (EventEncoder.cs:15-18) truncates the capture itself. The console JSONL record is then truncated. FileRuntimeStartupExpectations.cs:74 and verify-file-runtime-startup.py:69 expect it untruncated, with the exact full message and no truncated marker. So the unit, process and native consumers all fail this mode. The case also cannot show display-only loss as file-startup.md describes, because the loss comes from capture, not the file Human rendering.",
      "suggestedFix": "Give this mode a MaxEntryBytes between the captured JSONL size and the Human size. Human escapes U+200D as \\u200D (6 bytes; HumanText.cs:113-122), so Human is about 49 KB. 32768 works if the JSONL encoder writes the joiner raw (3 bytes each, about 24.6 KB). If JavaScriptEncoder escapes it to 6 bytes as well, JSONL and Human are the same size and no limit isolates Human loss; then use an input that only Human expands. Measure this before relying on it. Replace the loose 65536 cap with the configured value in FileRuntimeStartupExpectations.cs:71,74 and verify-file-runtime-startup.py:66,69. Keep the expected file Human record truncated and the console JSONL record untruncated. Then rerun the focused unit/process cases before the full and native runs."
